_comment: Candidate chat models for scripts/eval_models.py. Tags and sizes were read from the Ollama library pages on 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-02; licences are listed per entry. Published Hungarian evaluations exist and were consulted: the HuGME benchmark results (https://hugme.nytud.hu/Results/ ; it lists Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen3-4B, Gemma 3 4B/12B/27B and the Hungarian-primary Racka-4B, but covers language proficiency, knowledge and LLM-as-judge modules, not teaching-answer quality in a retrieval prompt) and OpenHuEval (https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.390.pdf, which includes Qwen2.5-7B). They are used as a hint for the list only; model-card language claims below remain unverified. Nothing here was run: whether a model teaches well in Hungarian, and whether it fits, is exactly what the run decides.

expected_fit is an estimate from the file size plus the evaluation context, for one GPU of typical consumer size; the run measures the real placement. Partial or multi-GPU placement is slower and depends on the link between the GPUs and on host RAM, which the run shows.
Copy this file outside the repo (or to a gitignored path) to change it.

candidates.expected_fit: single GPU likely, with room for the context
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 (7B size; the 3B and 72B sizes use other terms)
candidates.reason: Reference point. Broad multilingual instruct model with 32K context; Hungarian is not among the languages Qwen2.5 lists as supported, so its Hungarian is the question.

Qwen3 claims support for about 119 languages including Hungarian, a step up from Qwen2.5 on paper. It reasons in <think> blocks by default; the script strips them and sends think=false, which the Ollama version pinned in the compose file (0.6.6) may ignore, in which case the thinking tokens cost time. Needs Ollama 0.6.6 or newer.

candidates.expected_fit: single GPU likely, with long context to spare
candidates.license: Gemma Terms of Use (use restrictions apply; not an OSI open-source licence)
candidates.reason: Gemma 3 is trained on 140+ languages and is generally reported to be strong in smaller European languages for its size; the quantisation-aware tag keeps quality close to full precision. Needs Ollama 0.6.0 or newer.

candidates.expected_fit: single GPU likely, with long context to spare
candidates.license: CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 (non-commercial, share-alike): check it fits your use before relying on it
candidates.reason: Racka-4B is continually pretrained on Qwen3-4B with about 44% Hungarian data and a Hungarian-adapted tokenizer, from ELTE. The HuGME results list it with strong spelling and readability-type scores for its size but weak knowledge scores (MMLU, TruthfulQA), so it may write good Hungarian yet answer less reliably; the run shows which matters for grounded teaching. It is a base-style continued-pretraining model, so check that it follows the teacher prompt, JSON and citation rules.

candidates.role: likely best quality that is still local
candidates.expected_fit: a split across GPUs or partial CPU offload is likely on a small-VRAM GPU
candidates.license: Gemma Terms of Use (use restrictions apply; not an OSI open-source licence)
candidates.reason: The largest Gemma 3 that is realistic here. If it is clearly better in Hungarian than the 4B, the run shows what the split costs in time to first token and tokens per second. gemma3:12b-it-q4_K_M (8.2 GB) is the slightly smaller alternative.

candidates.expected_fit: weights alone nearly fill a small-VRAM GPU; a split or partial CPU offload is likely once the context is added
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 (from the model card; not shown on the Ollama page)
candidates.reason: Multilingual 12B from Mistral and NVIDIA with a large context window; Hungarian is not among its headline languages, so it is a test of a non-Qwen, non-Gemma family. q3_K_M (6.1 GB) would fit one GPU at some quality cost.

candidates.expected_fit: 12B-class: a split or partial offload is likely on a small-VRAM GPU
candidates.license: The page says Apache-2.0, but it is a fine-tune of Gemma 3, whose terms normally pass on to derivatives: treat it as Gemma Terms of Use until clarified
candidates.reason: Hungarian-tuned community chat model: a Gemma 3 fine-tune on Hungarian text, 128K context listed. It is a one-person upload with no published evaluation, so the run has to show whether it beats plain gemma3:12b. It ships its own default system prompt in Hungarian; the script sends the teacher prompt as the whole prompt.

not_selected.mp3pintyo/sambalingo-hungarian-chat: Hungarian chat model (Llama 2 based) but only a 4K context, too short for retrieval prompts.
not_selected.sony/puli-lliumix-32k: NYTK's Hungarian PULI LlumiX is a 13 GB base model, not an instruction/chat model.
not_selected.csabeszkukesz/qwen-hun-27b: Described as a Hungarian model (16 GB); unknown provenance and likely too large for one small-VRAM GPU.
not_selected.aya-expanse:8b: Hungarian is not among its 23 languages, and the licence is non-commercial.
not_selected.llama3.1:8b: Hungarian is not an officially supported language.
